stages.label: Stage 1
stages.deal_structure: Mostly cash at close under $1M; seller financing or earn-out common above that
stages.if_you_want_to_sell: At this size buyers pay a multiple of SDE and most deals close on marketplaces. A $300K ARR product with 30% SDE margin sells for 2x to 4x SDE, or $180K to $360K. The checklist items that move the price most are clean books, documented churn, and a product that runs without you.

stages.label: Stage 2
stages.deal_structure: 60% to 80% cash at close; seller note or earn-out for the balance
stages.if_you_want_to_sell: Buyers here pay 2.8x revenue at the median, or 4x to 8x SDE. A $1.2M ARR business with 35% SDE margin and 80%+ GRR sells for $1.7M to $3.4M. Growth above 30% and NRR above 100% push you to the top of the range.

stages.label: Stage 3
stages.deal_structure: 70% to 90% cash at close; rollover equity offered by PE
stages.if_you_want_to_sell: This is the first stage where PE and strategics compete for the deal. The median revenue multiple is 3.3x; top-quartile deals reach 7x. A $3.5M ARR company with 25% growth, 90% GRR and a GM in place can expect $10M to $15M. Without the GM, buyers add an earn-out.

stages.label: Stage 4
stages.valuation_method: EBITDA multiple or revenue multiple with Rule of 40
stages.deal_structure: Cash at close with 10% to 30% rollover for PE; escrow of 5% to 10%
stages.if_you_want_to_sell: Buyers run a full process with QoE and legal diligence. The median EBITDA multiple is 16.9x; revenue multiples run 2.9x at the median and above 9x for top-quartile growth and retention. An $8M ARR company that meets the Rule of 40 with 95% GRR can expect $25M to $50M.

stages.label: Stage 5
stages.valuation_method: EBITDA multiple or revenue multiple with Rule of 40
stages.revenue_multiple: No BVR band above $20M; use the $5M to $20M band as a floor and public comparables as a ceiling
stages.deal_structure: Cash at close; management rollover; representations and warranties insurance
stages.if_you_want_to_sell: Buyers at this size run a banker-led auction. Price depends on growth, NRR and the comparables in your category more than on any checklist item. The items here are the ones that keep the price intact through diligence.

scoring_rule.overrides: At stages 1 to 3, annual GRR under 70% or a 2 to 3 year ARR CAGR under 20% (or any flat or down year) makes the business difficult to sell, whatever the total.

detailed.note: Items as shown in the per-stage editions. Stages 4 and 5 use 4 compound foundations items.

items.item: Books are kept and closed at the standard your size requires

benchmarks.1: Cash basis is fine; books closed every quarter
benchmarks.2: Accrual basis; closed every quarter, monthly is better
benchmarks.3: Accrual basis; monthly close within 30 days

items.why_buyers_care: Buyers model future cash flow from closed, consistent books. Cash-basis books work under $500K; above that, accrual is what buyers expect.
items.concern_if_missing: Books that are not closed on a schedule cause restated numbers in diligence and a price cut.
items.what_to_strengthen: Close the books on a fixed schedule; move to accrual by $500K ARR and shorten the close as you grow.

items.item: Chart of accounts separates recurring revenue, services, and COGS (hosting, support, third-party tools)

benchmarks.1: Recurring, services, and COGS on separate lines for 12+ months
benchmarks.2: Recurring, services, and COGS on separate lines for 12+ months
benchmarks.3: Recurring, services, and COGS on separate lines for 12+ months

items.why_buyers_care: Buyers rebuild gross margin and recurring revenue percentage from your P&L. Mixed categories block that.
items.concern_if_missing: A buyer who cannot verify gross margin applies a lower multiple or asks for a Quality of Earnings at your cost.
items.what_to_strengthen: Build a SaaS chart of accounts with separate lines for subscription, services, and each COGS type.

items.item: Year-end financials prepared by a CPA, at the review level your size requires
items.why_buyers_care: Third-party financials cut diligence time and remove the first reason a buyer discounts your numbers.
items.concern_if_missing: Owner-prepared or unreviewed statements extend diligence by 4 to 8 weeks and invite a price adjustment.
items.what_to_strengthen: Engage a SaaS-experienced CPA; step up to review or audit as you grow.

items.item: Revenue is recognized over the contract term, with annual prepayments spread across 12 months

benchmarks.1: Monthly recognition; deferred revenue on the balance sheet
benchmarks.2: Monthly recognition; deferred revenue on the balance sheet
benchmarks.3: Monthly recognition; deferred revenue on the balance sheet

items.why_buyers_care: Buyers test revenue recognition first. Upfront booking of annual deals overstates revenue and understates deferred revenue.
items.concern_if_missing: Restated revenue in diligence lowers ARR, which lowers the price directly.
items.what_to_strengthen: Recognize subscription revenue monthly and carry prepaid amounts as deferred revenue.

items.item: ARR, churn, and customer counts in your billing or CRM system reconcile to the P&L
items.why_buyers_care: Buyers compare your metrics pack to your financials. A gap in either direction signals weak controls.
items.concern_if_missing: A reconciliation gap above 2% triggers a Quality of Earnings review and delays the deal.
items.what_to_strengthen: Reconcile billing system ARR to recognized revenue every quarter and document the differences.

items.item: Owner salary and personal expenses are tagged as add-backs with receipts
items.why_buyers_care: At this size buyers price on Seller's Discretionary Earnings. Every add-back needs proof.
items.concern_if_missing: Unsupported add-backs are removed from SDE, which cuts the price by the multiple times the add-back.
items.what_to_strengthen: Keep a running add-back schedule with the support document for each line.

items.item: All tax filings are current and every dollar of revenue runs through the books

benchmarks.1: All filings current; no off-book revenue
benchmarks.2: All filings current; no off-book revenue
benchmarks.3: All filings current; no off-book revenue
benchmarks.4: All filings current; no off-book revenue
benchmarks.5: All filings current; no off-book revenue

items.why_buyers_care: Buyers inherit tax exposure in a stock deal and discount it in an asset deal.
items.concern_if_missing: Late filings or off-book cash make the deal an asset sale with a holdback.
items.what_to_strengthen: Bring payroll, sales tax, and income tax filings current; close any off-book channel.

items.item: No cash-flow crisis in the past 24 months and at least 3 months of operating cash on hand
items.why_buyers_care: Buyers read cash history as a test of management. A crisis in the trailing period raises the risk premium.
items.concern_if_missing: A recent cash squeeze pushes buyers toward earn-outs instead of cash at close.
items.what_to_strengthen: Hold a cash reserve and track runway monthly.

items.item: A live financial dashboard tracks ARR, churn, cash, and margin by month

benchmarks.3: Monthly dashboard with 24 months of history
benchmarks.4: Monthly dashboard with 24 months of history
benchmarks.5: Monthly dashboard with 24 months of history

items.why_buyers_care: A dashboard that updates without you proves the business reports on itself.
items.concern_if_missing: Metrics assembled by hand for the deal look unreliable and take longer to verify.
items.what_to_strengthen: Connect billing and accounting to one dashboard and review it monthly with your team.

items.item: A 12-month budget exists and last year's actuals landed within 10% of plan
items.why_buyers_care: Buyers pay for a forecast they can trust. A track record of hitting plan supports forward multiples.
items.concern_if_missing: No budget or a large miss causes buyers to value the business on trailing numbers only.
items.what_to_strengthen: Build an annual budget, compare monthly, and document variances.

items.item: A Quality of Earnings report or QoE-style package is ready before you go to market

benchmarks.4: Sell-side QoE completed within the last 12 months
benchmarks.5: Sell-side QoE completed within the last 12 months

items.why_buyers_care: Institutional buyers commission a QoE. A sell-side QoE finds problems before they do and shortens diligence.
items.concern_if_missing: Buyer-side QoE findings become price reductions with no time for you to fix them.
items.what_to_strengthen: Commission a sell-side QoE 6 to 12 months before a sale.

items.item: Consistent historical financials cover the required number of years
items.why_buyers_care: Buyers want to see growth across multiple years, in one format, with no gaps.
items.concern_if_missing: Fewer than 2 years of clean history limits you to buyers who price on current ARR only.
items.what_to_strengthen: Restate earlier years into the current chart of accounts if needed.

items.item: Financial foundations are in place: accrual books, monthly close within 15 days, SaaS chart of accounts, monthly revenue recognition, deferred revenue tracked
items.why_buyers_care: At this size buyers assume these foundations exist. A missing one is a red flag, not a to-do.
items.concern_if_missing: A foundational gap at this size causes buyers to question every other number.
items.what_to_strengthen: Audit the basics with your CPA before you start a process.

items.item: Recurring revenue is the required share of total revenue
items.why_buyers_care: Recurring revenue is what buyers pay the SaaS multiple on. Services and one-time fees get a lower multiple or none.
items.concern_if_missing: Below 70% recurring, buyers value you as a services business.
items.what_to_strengthen: Productize services into subscriptions and separate one-time revenue in your reporting.

items.item: ARR growth, as a 2 to 3 year CAGR, meets the benchmark, and every year in that period grew
items.why_buyers_care: Growth is the largest single driver of the multiple. Buyers read a multi-year CAGR with steady years as proof of product-market fit; one strong year does not count.
items.concern_if_missing: Growth below 10% moves you from a growth multiple to a profit multiple.
items.what_to_strengthen: Track ARR growth monthly by cohort and segment; fix retention before you add acquisition spend.
items.warning: If your 2 to 3 year ARR CAGR is under 20%, or any year in that period was flat or down, buyers read it as a product-market fit problem. The business will be difficult to sell at this stage.

items.item: Gross revenue retention (annual) meets the benchmark
items.why_buyers_care: GRR shows how much revenue stays without any upsell. Buyers treat it as the core risk number.
items.concern_if_missing: GRR under 80% tells a buyer the product does not hold customers; expansion will not mask it.
items.what_to_strengthen: Track churn reasons, strengthen onboarding, and intervene on at-risk accounts.
items.warning: If your annual GRR is under 70%, the business will struggle to sell. Most buyers at this stage pass before they look at anything else.

items.item: Net revenue retention (annual) meets the benchmark
items.why_buyers_care: NRR above 100% means your customer base grows without new sales. It is the strongest proof of product value.
items.concern_if_missing: NRR under 90% means the revenue base shrinks; buyers price in continuous replacement cost.
items.what_to_strengthen: Add usage tiers or seat expansion and give customer success an expansion target.

items.item: Monthly logo churn is at or below the benchmark
items.why_buyers_care: Logo churn sets the customer lifetime, which sets LTV and the acquisition budget a buyer can justify.
items.concern_if_missing: Monthly churn above 5% means you lose half your customers each year.
items.what_to_strengthen: Segment churn by plan and acquisition channel, then cut the channels that bring churn-prone customers.

items.item: Pricing has at least 2 tiers or a usage path that lets customers spend more
items.why_buyers_care: Expansion revenue depends on a pricing model that allows it. Flat pricing caps NRR at 100%.
items.concern_if_missing: Single-tier pricing removes the expansion story from the buyer's model.
items.what_to_strengthen: Add a tier, a seat count, or a usage meter that scales with customer value.

items.item: Annual or multi-year contracts cover the required share of ARR
items.why_buyers_care: Contract term is the contractual floor under your revenue. Buyers model month-to-month revenue as at risk.
items.concern_if_missing: Month-to-month revenue lowers the revenue a buyer treats as committed.
items.what_to_strengthen: Offer a discount for annual prepay and renewals with auto-renew terms.

items.item: Cohort retention is tracked by month of acquisition
items.why_buyers_care: Cohorts show whether retention improves or decays as the product matures. A blended churn number hides this.
items.concern_if_missing: No cohort data makes a buyer assume the worst cohort is the trend.
items.what_to_strengthen: Build a monthly cohort table from billing data and keep 24 months of history.

items.item: Expansion ARR provides the required share of ARR growth
items.why_buyers_care: Growth from existing customers is cheaper and more predictable than growth from new logos.
items.concern_if_missing: Growth that comes only from new logos stops when marketing spend stops.
items.what_to_strengthen: Give account management an expansion quota and track upsell by cohort.

items.item: Failed-payment recovery is automated

benchmarks.1: Dunning live; involuntary churn under 1% monthly
benchmarks.2: Dunning live; involuntary churn under 1% monthly
benchmarks.3: Dunning live; involuntary churn under 1% monthly

items.why_buyers_care: Involuntary churn is the cheapest churn to fix. Buyers see unfixed dunning as neglect.
items.concern_if_missing: Unrecovered failed payments inflate churn and lower both GRR and NRR.
items.what_to_strengthen: Turn on dunning in your billing system and retry failed cards for 21 days.

items.item: Gross margin meets the benchmark with hosting, support, and onboarding in COGS
items.why_buyers_care: Gross margin sets how much of each new dollar becomes profit. Buyers test it against the 70 to 80% SaaS norm.
items.concern_if_missing: Gross margin under 60% means the buyer values you as a services business.
items.what_to_strengthen: Move support and onboarding into COGS, then cut hosting cost and automate onboarding.

items.item: LTV to CAC ratio is tracked and meets the benchmark
items.why_buyers_care: LTV:CAC tells a buyer whether growth spend pays back. It is the efficiency number behind the growth number.
items.concern_if_missing: A ratio under 2x means the buyer must cut marketing to make the business profitable.
items.what_to_strengthen: Compute LTV on gross profit, include commissions and onboarding in CAC, and review by channel.

items.item: CAC payback period is at or under the benchmark
items.why_buyers_care: Payback sets how much cash growth consumes. Buyers with a growth plan need payback they can fund.
items.concern_if_missing: Payback over 24 months means growth needs outside capital.
items.what_to_strengthen: Raise prices, improve conversion, and shorten time to first value.

items.item: Profitability meets the benchmark for your size and valuation method

benchmarks.3: EBITDA margin 10%+ or Rule of 40 met

items.why_buyers_care: Below $2M buyers pay on SDE. Above $5M they pay on EBITDA or on growth under the Rule of 40.
items.concern_if_missing: Negative profit with growth under 20% leaves no valuation method that supports a premium.
items.what_to_strengthen: Audit spend by department and set a margin target that fits your growth rate.

items.item: ARR per employee meets the benchmark
items.why_buyers_care: ARR per employee is the fastest read on operating leverage. Low numbers signal a services-heavy model.
items.concern_if_missing: Under $200K per employee tells a buyer the margin will not expand with scale.
items.what_to_strengthen: Automate support and onboarding and hold headcount growth below ARR growth.

items.item: Sales and marketing spend is tracked by channel with cost per customer
items.why_buyers_care: Buyers want to know which channels work so they can add capital to them.
items.concern_if_missing: Blended CAC without channel detail blocks the buyer's growth model.
items.what_to_strengthen: Tag every new customer with its source and compute CAC per channel quarterly.

items.item: Customer concentration is below the benchmark
items.why_buyers_care: One lost customer should not change the price. Buyers discount concentrated revenue or ask for an earn-out on it.
items.concern_if_missing: Top 5 customers above 50% of revenue is a high-risk flag in every buyer's model.
items.what_to_strengthen: Diversify go-to-market and lock large accounts into multi-year contracts.

items.item: One system holds every customer with MRR, start date, plan, and contract
items.why_buyers_care: The customer list is the first diligence request. It must tie to billing and to the P&L.
items.concern_if_missing: A customer list assembled by hand for the deal takes weeks and rarely ties out.
items.what_to_strengthen: Keep the billing system or CRM as the single source and export it monthly.

items.item: Largest customers are on written contracts that allow assignment on a change of control
items.why_buyers_care: A buyer needs the contracts to transfer. Consent clauses give customers a chance to renegotiate at close.
items.concern_if_missing: Contracts that block assignment delay closing and give key customers leverage.
items.what_to_strengthen: Standardize terms and amend the largest contracts before you go to market.

items.item: Customer satisfaction is measured at least once a year (NPS or survey)
items.why_buyers_care: Satisfaction data predicts retention before churn shows up in the numbers.
items.concern_if_missing: No satisfaction data leaves the buyer to assume churn will rise after the owner leaves.
items.what_to_strengthen: Run an annual NPS survey and track the score by segment.

items.item: Support runs on a documented process with a named owner who is not the founder
items.why_buyers_care: Support is where founder dependence shows up first. Buyers test whether customers rely on you personally.
items.concern_if_missing: Founder-run support means customer relationships leave with the founder.
items.what_to_strengthen: Appoint a support owner, document the process, and track response time.

items.item: Onboarding is productized, with self-serve steps where possible

benchmarks.1: Documented onboarding; under 5 founder hours per customer
benchmarks.2: Documented onboarding; under 5 founder hours per customer
benchmarks.3: Documented onboarding; under 5 founder hours per customer

items.why_buyers_care: Onboarding cost sits in gross margin, and onboarding quality sets early churn.
items.concern_if_missing: Hands-on onboarding by the founder lowers margin and does not scale for a buyer.
items.what_to_strengthen: Write the onboarding checklist and automate the first 3 steps.

items.item: A customer success function owns renewals and expansion

benchmarks.4: CS lead with renewal and expansion targets
benchmarks.5: CS lead with renewal and expansion targets

items.why_buyers_care: At this size buyers expect a team that drives NRR, not an inbox.
items.concern_if_missing: No CS function caps NRR and makes the growth plan depend on new logos.
items.what_to_strengthen: Hire or assign a CS lead with a renewal and expansion quota.

items.item: The founder can leave for the benchmark period with no drop in revenue or service
items.why_buyers_care: If the business cannot run without you, a buyer is buying a job. Transferability sets the multiple.
items.concern_if_missing: High owner dependence moves buyers to an earn-out and a long transition period.
items.what_to_strengthen: Take a planned absence, log what breaks, and fix each item.

items.item: At least 2 people can deploy to production and fix a critical bug

benchmarks.1: 2+ people with production access and runbook
benchmarks.2: 2+ people with production access and runbook
benchmarks.3: 2+ people with production access and runbook

items.why_buyers_care: A single engineer who holds the system is a key-person risk buyers price in.
items.concern_if_missing: One-person technical knowledge becomes a retention condition in the deal.
items.what_to_strengthen: Cross-train a second engineer and document the deployment runbook.

items.item: Sales closes without the founder at the required level

benchmarks.3: A sales lead owns the pipeline
benchmarks.4: Sales leader and team; founder in under 10% of deals
benchmarks.5: Sales leader and team; founder in under 10% of deals

items.why_buyers_care: If every deal needs the founder, revenue growth is tied to the founder's hours.
items.concern_if_missing: Founder-led sales is the most common reason buyers cut the price of a $2M to $10M SaaS.
items.what_to_strengthen: Hire a seller, write the sales process, and move the founder out of first calls.

items.item: Every role has a written description and the core processes have SOPs in cloud storage

benchmarks.1: Role descriptions and SOPs for all recurring processes
benchmarks.2: Role descriptions and SOPs for all recurring processes
benchmarks.3: Role descriptions and SOPs for all recurring processes

items.why_buyers_care: Documentation is how a buyer takes over operations without you.
items.concern_if_missing: No documentation extends the transition period and the earn-out.
items.what_to_strengthen: Write one SOP per recurring process and store them where the team works.

items.item: A second-in-command or general manager runs day-to-day operations

benchmarks.3: GM or COO in place 6+ months
benchmarks.4: GM or COO in place 12+ months
benchmarks.5: GM or COO in place 12+ months

items.why_buyers_care: Buyers need a leader who stays. The founder usually leaves within 12 months of a sale.
items.concern_if_missing: No number two means the buyer has to hire one and prices that risk in.
items.what_to_strengthen: Promote or hire a GM and hand over operations 12 months before a sale.

items.item: A leadership team covers product, engineering, sales, and finance
items.why_buyers_care: At this size buyers evaluate the team as much as the numbers.
items.concern_if_missing: Gaps in the leadership team lower the multiple and extend the founder's required stay.
items.what_to_strengthen: Fill each function with a leader who has SaaS experience.

items.item: Key employees have employment agreements and a retention or equity plan

benchmarks.4: Agreements, retention plan, and option pool
benchmarks.5: Agreements, retention plan, and option pool

items.why_buyers_care: Buyers want the people who built the product to stay through the transition.
items.concern_if_missing: Unretained key staff become a closing condition or a holdback.
items.what_to_strengthen: Put key people on agreements with a retention bonus that vests after close.

items.item: An org chart shows every role and reporting line
items.why_buyers_care: The org chart is the buyer's map of who does what and where the founder sits.
items.concern_if_missing: No org chart signals that the founder holds the structure in their head.
items.what_to_strengthen: Draw the chart, include contractors, and update it quarterly.

items.item: Hiring and onboarding follow a documented process
items.why_buyers_care: A buyer who plans to grow needs to hire without you.
items.concern_if_missing: Ad-hoc hiring means the growth plan depends on the founder's network.
items.what_to_strengthen: Document the hiring steps and the 30-day onboarding plan for each role type.

items.item: Operational foundations are in place: role descriptions, SOPs, 2+ people on production, productized onboarding
items.why_buyers_care: At this size buyers assume these foundations exist. A missing one is a red flag, not a to-do.
items.concern_if_missing: A foundational gap at this size causes buyers to question how the company scaled.
items.what_to_strengthen: Audit the basics with your GM before you start a process.

items.item: The product is cloud-hosted and multi-tenant, with no on-premise installs
items.why_buyers_care: Delivery model sets margin and scalability. Buyers pay the SaaS multiple for cloud-native products.
items.concern_if_missing: On-prem or single-tenant installs move you toward a software license multiple.
items.what_to_strengthen: Migrate remaining installs to the cloud platform and sunset the legacy option.

items.item: Code is in version control with a repeatable deployment and automated tests

benchmarks.3: CI/CD and test coverage on critical paths

items.why_buyers_care: Technical diligence starts with the repo. Buyers look for process, not perfection.
items.concern_if_missing: No tests or manual deploys raise the technical risk score and the integration cost.
items.what_to_strengthen: Set up CI/CD and cover the critical paths with automated tests.

items.item: Architecture and operations are documented well enough for a new engineer to deploy within a week
items.why_buyers_care: Documentation is how the buyer's team takes over the codebase.
items.concern_if_missing: Undocumented systems extend the founder's required stay.
items.what_to_strengthen: Write the architecture overview, the runbooks, and the environment setup guide.

items.item: Third-party dependencies and open-source licenses are inventoried

benchmarks.2: License inventory current; no unresolved copyleft
benchmarks.3: License inventory current; no unresolved copyleft
benchmarks.4: License inventory current; no unresolved copyleft
benchmarks.5: License inventory current; no unresolved copyleft

items.why_buyers_care: Buyers scan for copyleft licenses and unlicensed components. A finding can block a stock deal.
items.concern_if_missing: An unknown GPL dependency in the core product is a closing condition.
items.what_to_strengthen: Run a license scan and resolve any copyleft or unlicensed component.

items.item: Security meets the benchmark for your size

benchmarks.3: Security policy and annual penetration test

items.why_buyers_care: Security findings in diligence become price reductions or indemnities.
items.concern_if_missing: No security controls at any size is a deal risk; no SOC 2 above $5M blocks many buyers.
items.what_to_strengthen: Start with MFA, backups, and access control; add a penetration test and SOC 2 as you grow.

items.item: Uptime is tracked and meets the benchmark
items.why_buyers_care: Reliability is a retention driver and a contractual obligation in enterprise deals.
items.concern_if_missing: No uptime record means the buyer cannot verify the SLA you sell.
items.what_to_strengthen: Add monitoring and publish uptime to customers.

items.item: A written 12-month product roadmap exists
items.why_buyers_care: The roadmap is the buyer's view of where growth comes from after close.
items.concern_if_missing: No roadmap means the buyer values the product as it is today.
items.what_to_strengthen: Write a 12-month roadmap tied to retention and expansion goals.

items.item: Differentiation is evidenced with win/loss data or documented reasons customers chose you
items.why_buyers_care: Buyers pay a premium for a product that is hard to replace. Claims need evidence.
items.concern_if_missing: Differentiation without evidence reads as marketing, not as a moat.
items.what_to_strengthen: Track win/loss reasons in the CRM and collect 5 customer quotes on why they switched.

items.item: Integrations or an API create switching costs

benchmarks.3: 3+ live integrations or a public API
benchmarks.4: 3+ live integrations or a public API
benchmarks.5: 3+ live integrations or a public API

items.why_buyers_care: Switching costs protect retention and pricing. Buyers model them as a retention floor.
items.concern_if_missing: A product with no integrations is easier to replace at renewal.
items.what_to_strengthen: Build the 3 integrations your customers ask for most and publish an API.

items.item: Technical foundations are in place: cloud-hosted, CI/CD, automated tests, 2+ engineers on production
items.why_buyers_care: At this size buyers assume these foundations exist. A missing one is a red flag, not a to-do.
items.concern_if_missing: A foundational gap at this size raises the technical risk score for the whole platform.
items.what_to_strengthen: Run an internal technical audit before you start a process.

items.item: The ideal customer profile is written down with segment, size, and average contract value

benchmarks.1: ICP documented; 70%+ of new customers match
benchmarks.2: ICP documented; 70%+ of new customers match
benchmarks.3: ICP documented; 70%+ of new customers match
benchmarks.4: ICP documented; 70%+ of new customers match
benchmarks.5: ICP documented; 70%+ of new customers match

items.why_buyers_care: A clear ICP lets a buyer judge the market and the growth plan. It also explains your churn.
items.concern_if_missing: No ICP means the buyer cannot size the opportunity or trust the CAC.
items.what_to_strengthen: Write a 1-page ICP and check that 70%+ of new customers match it.

items.item: A bottom-up TAM and SAM exist with sources
items.why_buyers_care: Buyers pay for headroom. A small or vague TAM caps the multiple even with strong metrics.
items.concern_if_missing: Top-down TAM from a market report is discounted; bottom-up numbers are trusted.
items.what_to_strengthen: Build TAM from ICP count times ACV and cite the sources.

items.item: Market growth is cited from a third-party source

benchmarks.3: 10%+ market growth with a cited source
benchmarks.4: 10%+ market growth with a cited source
benchmarks.5: 10%+ market growth with a cited source

items.why_buyers_care: A growing market gives the buyer tailwind for the growth plan.
items.concern_if_missing: Founder estimates of market growth are not used in buyer models.
items.what_to_strengthen: Cite a Gartner, Forrester, or PitchBook growth rate for your segment.

items.item: Named competitors and your position against them are documented, with win rate

benchmarks.3: Competitor map and 12 months of win rate
benchmarks.4: Competitor map and 12 months of win rate
benchmarks.5: Competitor map and 12 months of win rate

items.why_buyers_care: Buyers want to know who you beat and why. Win rate is the proof.
items.concern_if_missing: No competitive data means the buyer runs their own analysis and prices the unknown.
items.what_to_strengthen: Keep a competitor map and track win rate against each named competitor.

items.item: Recent acquisitions in your category are tracked
items.why_buyers_care: Buyer activity in your category sets the comparable multiples.
items.concern_if_missing: No comparables leaves the buyer to anchor on a generic SaaS multiple.
items.what_to_strengthen: Keep a list of the last 10 deals in your category with price and multiple where public.

items.item: The company is a corporation or LLC with a clean cap table and current founder agreements

benchmarks.1: Cap table and founder agreements current
benchmarks.2: Cap table and founder agreements current
benchmarks.3: Cap table and founder agreements current

items.why_buyers_care: Buyers buy a legal entity. Ownership must be clear before a letter of intent.
items.concern_if_missing: Unclear ownership or a missing founder agreement stops the deal at diligence.
items.what_to_strengthen: Confirm the cap table with counsel and sign any missing founder or shareholder agreement.

items.item: Every employee and contractor who wrote code has signed an IP assignment
items.why_buyers_care: Without IP assignment the company does not own its own product.
items.concern_if_missing: One missing assignment from an early contractor is a closing condition and a holdback.
items.what_to_strengthen: Audit contributors and collect signed assignments from each one.

items.item: Terms of service, privacy policy, and data processing terms are current
items.why_buyers_care: Customer terms set what the buyer inherits, including liability and data rights.
items.concern_if_missing: Outdated terms raise privacy liability and may block enterprise customers from transferring.
items.what_to_strengthen: Update terms with counsel and have every customer accept the current version.

items.item: Trademarks are registered and all domains are owned by the company

benchmarks.2: Mark registered; domains in company account
benchmarks.3: Mark registered; domains in company account
benchmarks.4: Mark registered; domains in company account
benchmarks.5: Mark registered; domains in company account

items.why_buyers_care: Brand assets must transfer with the company.
items.concern_if_missing: A domain in the founder's personal account becomes a transfer item at close.
items.what_to_strengthen: Register the mark and move domains into a company-owned account.

items.item: No open litigation, claims, or regulatory issues
items.why_buyers_care: Buyers price open claims at the worst case and ask for an indemnity.
items.concern_if_missing: Any open claim becomes an escrow at close.
items.what_to_strengthen: Settle or document every open matter before you go to market.

items.item: Vendor and partner contracts are assignable on a change of control
items.why_buyers_care: Critical vendors who can terminate at close give them leverage over your deal.
items.concern_if_missing: A non-assignable hosting or data contract is a closing condition.
items.what_to_strengthen: Review the top 10 vendor contracts and amend the change-of-control clauses.

items.item: Compliance obligations for your vertical are met (GDPR, HIPAA, PCI, or others that apply)

benchmarks.3: Compliance map current; no open gaps
benchmarks.4: Compliance map current; no open gaps
benchmarks.5: Compliance map current; no open gaps

items.why_buyers_care: Regulatory gaps are indemnity items. Enterprise buyers verify them before the LOI.
items.concern_if_missing: A compliance gap in a regulated vertical removes strategic buyers from the process.
items.what_to_strengthen: Map the regulations that apply and close each gap with counsel.

items.item: A data inventory shows where customer data lives and who can access it
items.why_buyers_care: Data diligence asks this question first. The answer sets the privacy risk.
items.concern_if_missing: Unknown data locations extend diligence and raise the privacy indemnity.
items.what_to_strengthen: Document every system that holds customer data and the access list for each.

items.item: Legal foundations are in place: clean cap table, current customer terms, no open claims
items.why_buyers_care: At this size buyers assume these foundations exist. A missing one is a red flag, not a to-do.
items.concern_if_missing: A foundational legal gap at this size delays the LOI.
items.what_to_strengthen: Have counsel run a pre-sale legal audit.

master.note: Items as shown in the master checklist. Foundations expanded into their underlying items at stages 4 and 5.

items.item: Books are kept and closed at the standard your size requires

benchmarks.1: Cash basis is fine; books closed every quarter
benchmarks.2: Accrual basis; closed every quarter, monthly is better
benchmarks.3: Accrual basis; monthly close within 30 days

items.why_buyers_care: Buyers model future cash flow from closed, consistent books. Cash-basis books work under $500K; above that, accrual is what buyers expect.
items.concern_if_missing: Books that are not closed on a schedule cause restated numbers in diligence and a price cut.
items.what_to_strengthen: Close the books on a fixed schedule; move to accrual by $500K ARR and shorten the close as you grow.

items.item: Chart of accounts separates recurring revenue, services, and COGS (hosting, support, third-party tools)

benchmarks.1: Recurring, services, and COGS on separate lines for 12+ months
benchmarks.2: Recurring, services, and COGS on separate lines for 12+ months
benchmarks.3: Recurring, services, and COGS on separate lines for 12+ months

items.why_buyers_care: Buyers rebuild gross margin and recurring revenue percentage from your P&L. Mixed categories block that.
items.concern_if_missing: A buyer who cannot verify gross margin applies a lower multiple or asks for a Quality of Earnings at your cost.
items.what_to_strengthen: Build a SaaS chart of accounts with separate lines for subscription, services, and each COGS type.

items.item: Year-end financials prepared by a CPA, at the review level your size requires
items.why_buyers_care: Third-party financials cut diligence time and remove the first reason a buyer discounts your numbers.
items.concern_if_missing: Owner-prepared or unreviewed statements extend diligence by 4 to 8 weeks and invite a price adjustment.
items.what_to_strengthen: Engage a SaaS-experienced CPA; step up to review or audit as you grow.

items.item: Revenue is recognized over the contract term, with annual prepayments spread across 12 months

benchmarks.1: Monthly recognition; deferred revenue on the balance sheet
benchmarks.2: Monthly recognition; deferred revenue on the balance sheet
benchmarks.3: Monthly recognition; deferred revenue on the balance sheet

items.why_buyers_care: Buyers test revenue recognition first. Upfront booking of annual deals overstates revenue and understates deferred revenue.
items.concern_if_missing: Restated revenue in diligence lowers ARR, which lowers the price directly.
items.what_to_strengthen: Recognize subscription revenue monthly and carry prepaid amounts as deferred revenue.

items.item: ARR, churn, and customer counts in your billing or CRM system reconcile to the P&L
items.why_buyers_care: Buyers compare your metrics pack to your financials. A gap in either direction signals weak controls.
items.concern_if_missing: A reconciliation gap above 2% triggers a Quality of Earnings review and delays the deal.
items.what_to_strengthen: Reconcile billing system ARR to recognized revenue every quarter and document the differences.

items.item: Owner salary and personal expenses are tagged as add-backs with receipts
items.why_buyers_care: At this size buyers price on Seller's Discretionary Earnings. Every add-back needs proof.
items.concern_if_missing: Unsupported add-backs are removed from SDE, which cuts the price by the multiple times the add-back.
items.what_to_strengthen: Keep a running add-back schedule with the support document for each line.

items.item: All tax filings are current and every dollar of revenue runs through the books

benchmarks.1: All filings current; no off-book revenue
benchmarks.2: All filings current; no off-book revenue
benchmarks.3: All filings current; no off-book revenue
benchmarks.4: All filings current; no off-book revenue
benchmarks.5: All filings current; no off-book revenue

items.why_buyers_care: Buyers inherit tax exposure in a stock deal and discount it in an asset deal.
items.concern_if_missing: Late filings or off-book cash make the deal an asset sale with a holdback.
items.what_to_strengthen: Bring payroll, sales tax, and income tax filings current; close any off-book channel.

items.item: No cash-flow crisis in the past 24 months and at least 3 months of operating cash on hand
items.why_buyers_care: Buyers read cash history as a test of management. A crisis in the trailing period raises the risk premium.
items.concern_if_missing: A recent cash squeeze pushes buyers toward earn-outs instead of cash at close.
items.what_to_strengthen: Hold a cash reserve and track runway monthly.

items.item: A live financial dashboard tracks ARR, churn, cash, and margin by month

benchmarks.3: Monthly dashboard with 24 months of history
benchmarks.4: Monthly dashboard with 24 months of history
benchmarks.5: Monthly dashboard with 24 months of history

items.why_buyers_care: A dashboard that updates without you proves the business reports on itself.
items.concern_if_missing: Metrics assembled by hand for the deal look unreliable and take longer to verify.
items.what_to_strengthen: Connect billing and accounting to one dashboard and review it monthly with your team.

items.item: A 12-month budget exists and last year's actuals landed within 10% of plan
items.why_buyers_care: Buyers pay for a forecast they can trust. A track record of hitting plan supports forward multiples.
items.concern_if_missing: No budget or a large miss causes buyers to value the business on trailing numbers only.
items.what_to_strengthen: Build an annual budget, compare monthly, and document variances.

items.item: A Quality of Earnings report or QoE-style package is ready before you go to market

benchmarks.4: Sell-side QoE completed within the last 12 months
benchmarks.5: Sell-side QoE completed within the last 12 months

items.why_buyers_care: Institutional buyers commission a QoE. A sell-side QoE finds problems before they do and shortens diligence.
items.concern_if_missing: Buyer-side QoE findings become price reductions with no time for you to fix them.
items.what_to_strengthen: Commission a sell-side QoE 6 to 12 months before a sale.

items.item: Consistent historical financials cover the required number of years
items.why_buyers_care: Buyers want to see growth across multiple years, in one format, with no gaps.
items.concern_if_missing: Fewer than 2 years of clean history limits you to buyers who price on current ARR only.
items.what_to_strengthen: Restate earlier years into the current chart of accounts if needed.

items.item: Recurring revenue is the required share of total revenue
items.why_buyers_care: Recurring revenue is what buyers pay the SaaS multiple on. Services and one-time fees get a lower multiple or none.
items.concern_if_missing: Below 70% recurring, buyers value you as a services business.
items.what_to_strengthen: Productize services into subscriptions and separate one-time revenue in your reporting.

items.item: ARR growth, as a 2 to 3 year CAGR, meets the benchmark, and every year in that period grew
items.why_buyers_care: Growth is the largest single driver of the multiple. Buyers read a multi-year CAGR with steady years as proof of product-market fit; one strong year does not count.
items.concern_if_missing: Growth below 10% moves you from a growth multiple to a profit multiple.
items.what_to_strengthen: Track ARR growth monthly by cohort and segment; fix retention before you add acquisition spend.
items.warning: If your 2 to 3 year ARR CAGR is under 20%, or any year in that period was flat or down, buyers read it as a product-market fit problem. The business will be difficult to sell at this stage.

items.item: Gross revenue retention (annual) meets the benchmark
items.why_buyers_care: GRR shows how much revenue stays without any upsell. Buyers treat it as the core risk number.
items.concern_if_missing: GRR under 80% tells a buyer the product does not hold customers; expansion will not mask it.
items.what_to_strengthen: Track churn reasons, strengthen onboarding, and intervene on at-risk accounts.
items.warning: If your annual GRR is under 70%, the business will struggle to sell. Most buyers at this stage pass before they look at anything else.

items.item: Net revenue retention (annual) meets the benchmark
items.why_buyers_care: NRR above 100% means your customer base grows without new sales. It is the strongest proof of product value.
items.concern_if_missing: NRR under 90% means the revenue base shrinks; buyers price in continuous replacement cost.
items.what_to_strengthen: Add usage tiers or seat expansion and give customer success an expansion target.

items.item: Monthly logo churn is at or below the benchmark
items.why_buyers_care: Logo churn sets the customer lifetime, which sets LTV and the acquisition budget a buyer can justify.
items.concern_if_missing: Monthly churn above 5% means you lose half your customers each year.
items.what_to_strengthen: Segment churn by plan and acquisition channel, then cut the channels that bring churn-prone customers.

items.item: Pricing has at least 2 tiers or a usage path that lets customers spend more
items.why_buyers_care: Expansion revenue depends on a pricing model that allows it. Flat pricing caps NRR at 100%.
items.concern_if_missing: Single-tier pricing removes the expansion story from the buyer's model.
items.what_to_strengthen: Add a tier, a seat count, or a usage meter that scales with customer value.

items.item: Annual or multi-year contracts cover the required share of ARR
items.why_buyers_care: Contract term is the contractual floor under your revenue. Buyers model month-to-month revenue as at risk.
items.concern_if_missing: Month-to-month revenue lowers the revenue a buyer treats as committed.
items.what_to_strengthen: Offer a discount for annual prepay and renewals with auto-renew terms.

items.item: Cohort retention is tracked by month of acquisition
items.why_buyers_care: Cohorts show whether retention improves or decays as the product matures. A blended churn number hides this.
items.concern_if_missing: No cohort data makes a buyer assume the worst cohort is the trend.
items.what_to_strengthen: Build a monthly cohort table from billing data and keep 24 months of history.

items.item: Expansion ARR provides the required share of ARR growth
items.why_buyers_care: Growth from existing customers is cheaper and more predictable than growth from new logos.
items.concern_if_missing: Growth that comes only from new logos stops when marketing spend stops.
items.what_to_strengthen: Give account management an expansion quota and track upsell by cohort.

items.item: Failed-payment recovery is automated

benchmarks.1: Dunning live; involuntary churn under 1% monthly
benchmarks.2: Dunning live; involuntary churn under 1% monthly
benchmarks.3: Dunning live; involuntary churn under 1% monthly

items.why_buyers_care: Involuntary churn is the cheapest churn to fix. Buyers see unfixed dunning as neglect.
items.concern_if_missing: Unrecovered failed payments inflate churn and lower both GRR and NRR.
items.what_to_strengthen: Turn on dunning in your billing system and retry failed cards for 21 days.

items.item: Gross margin meets the benchmark with hosting, support, and onboarding in COGS
items.why_buyers_care: Gross margin sets how much of each new dollar becomes profit. Buyers test it against the 70 to 80% SaaS norm.
items.concern_if_missing: Gross margin under 60% means the buyer values you as a services business.
items.what_to_strengthen: Move support and onboarding into COGS, then cut hosting cost and automate onboarding.

items.item: LTV to CAC ratio is tracked and meets the benchmark
items.why_buyers_care: LTV:CAC tells a buyer whether growth spend pays back. It is the efficiency number behind the growth number.
items.concern_if_missing: A ratio under 2x means the buyer must cut marketing to make the business profitable.
items.what_to_strengthen: Compute LTV on gross profit, include commissions and onboarding in CAC, and review by channel.

items.item: CAC payback period is at or under the benchmark
items.why_buyers_care: Payback sets how much cash growth consumes. Buyers with a growth plan need payback they can fund.
items.concern_if_missing: Payback over 24 months means growth needs outside capital.
items.what_to_strengthen: Raise prices, improve conversion, and shorten time to first value.

items.item: Profitability meets the benchmark for your size and valuation method

benchmarks.3: EBITDA margin 10%+ or Rule of 40 met

items.why_buyers_care: Below $2M buyers pay on SDE. Above $5M they pay on EBITDA or on growth under the Rule of 40.
items.concern_if_missing: Negative profit with growth under 20% leaves no valuation method that supports a premium.
items.what_to_strengthen: Audit spend by department and set a margin target that fits your growth rate.

items.item: ARR per employee meets the benchmark
items.why_buyers_care: ARR per employee is the fastest read on operating leverage. Low numbers signal a services-heavy model.
items.concern_if_missing: Under $200K per employee tells a buyer the margin will not expand with scale.
items.what_to_strengthen: Automate support and onboarding and hold headcount growth below ARR growth.

items.item: Sales and marketing spend is tracked by channel with cost per customer
items.why_buyers_care: Buyers want to know which channels work so they can add capital to them.
items.concern_if_missing: Blended CAC without channel detail blocks the buyer's growth model.
items.what_to_strengthen: Tag every new customer with its source and compute CAC per channel quarterly.

items.item: Customer concentration is below the benchmark
items.why_buyers_care: One lost customer should not change the price. Buyers discount concentrated revenue or ask for an earn-out on it.
items.concern_if_missing: Top 5 customers above 50% of revenue is a high-risk flag in every buyer's model.
items.what_to_strengthen: Diversify go-to-market and lock large accounts into multi-year contracts.

items.item: One system holds every customer with MRR, start date, plan, and contract
items.why_buyers_care: The customer list is the first diligence request. It must tie to billing and to the P&L.
items.concern_if_missing: A customer list assembled by hand for the deal takes weeks and rarely ties out.
items.what_to_strengthen: Keep the billing system or CRM as the single source and export it monthly.

items.item: Largest customers are on written contracts that allow assignment on a change of control
items.why_buyers_care: A buyer needs the contracts to transfer. Consent clauses give customers a chance to renegotiate at close.
items.concern_if_missing: Contracts that block assignment delay closing and give key customers leverage.
items.what_to_strengthen: Standardize terms and amend the largest contracts before you go to market.

items.item: Customer satisfaction is measured at least once a year (NPS or survey)
items.why_buyers_care: Satisfaction data predicts retention before churn shows up in the numbers.
items.concern_if_missing: No satisfaction data leaves the buyer to assume churn will rise after the owner leaves.
items.what_to_strengthen: Run an annual NPS survey and track the score by segment.

items.item: Support runs on a documented process with a named owner who is not the founder
items.why_buyers_care: Support is where founder dependence shows up first. Buyers test whether customers rely on you personally.
items.concern_if_missing: Founder-run support means customer relationships leave with the founder.
items.what_to_strengthen: Appoint a support owner, document the process, and track response time.

items.item: Onboarding is productized, with self-serve steps where possible

benchmarks.1: Documented onboarding; under 5 founder hours per customer
benchmarks.2: Documented onboarding; under 5 founder hours per customer
benchmarks.3: Documented onboarding; under 5 founder hours per customer

items.why_buyers_care: Onboarding cost sits in gross margin, and onboarding quality sets early churn.
items.concern_if_missing: Hands-on onboarding by the founder lowers margin and does not scale for a buyer.
items.what_to_strengthen: Write the onboarding checklist and automate the first 3 steps.

items.item: A customer success function owns renewals and expansion

benchmarks.4: CS lead with renewal and expansion targets
benchmarks.5: CS lead with renewal and expansion targets

items.why_buyers_care: At this size buyers expect a team that drives NRR, not an inbox.
items.concern_if_missing: No CS function caps NRR and makes the growth plan depend on new logos.
items.what_to_strengthen: Hire or assign a CS lead with a renewal and expansion quota.

items.item: The founder can leave for the benchmark period with no drop in revenue or service
items.why_buyers_care: If the business cannot run without you, a buyer is buying a job. Transferability sets the multiple.
items.concern_if_missing: High owner dependence moves buyers to an earn-out and a long transition period.
items.what_to_strengthen: Take a planned absence, log what breaks, and fix each item.

items.item: At least 2 people can deploy to production and fix a critical bug

benchmarks.1: 2+ people with production access and runbook
benchmarks.2: 2+ people with production access and runbook
benchmarks.3: 2+ people with production access and runbook

items.why_buyers_care: A single engineer who holds the system is a key-person risk buyers price in.
items.concern_if_missing: One-person technical knowledge becomes a retention condition in the deal.
items.what_to_strengthen: Cross-train a second engineer and document the deployment runbook.

items.item: Sales closes without the founder at the required level

benchmarks.3: A sales lead owns the pipeline
benchmarks.4: Sales leader and team; founder in under 10% of deals
benchmarks.5: Sales leader and team; founder in under 10% of deals

items.why_buyers_care: If every deal needs the founder, revenue growth is tied to the founder's hours.
items.concern_if_missing: Founder-led sales is the most common reason buyers cut the price of a $2M to $10M SaaS.
items.what_to_strengthen: Hire a seller, write the sales process, and move the founder out of first calls.

items.item: Every role has a written description and the core processes have SOPs in cloud storage

benchmarks.1: Role descriptions and SOPs for all recurring processes
benchmarks.2: Role descriptions and SOPs for all recurring processes
benchmarks.3: Role descriptions and SOPs for all recurring processes

items.why_buyers_care: Documentation is how a buyer takes over operations without you.
items.concern_if_missing: No documentation extends the transition period and the earn-out.
items.what_to_strengthen: Write one SOP per recurring process and store them where the team works.

items.item: A second-in-command or general manager runs day-to-day operations

benchmarks.3: GM or COO in place 6+ months
benchmarks.4: GM or COO in place 12+ months
benchmarks.5: GM or COO in place 12+ months

items.why_buyers_care: Buyers need a leader who stays. The founder usually leaves within 12 months of a sale.
items.concern_if_missing: No number two means the buyer has to hire one and prices that risk in.
items.what_to_strengthen: Promote or hire a GM and hand over operations 12 months before a sale.

items.item: A leadership team covers product, engineering, sales, and finance
items.why_buyers_care: At this size buyers evaluate the team as much as the numbers.
items.concern_if_missing: Gaps in the leadership team lower the multiple and extend the founder's required stay.
items.what_to_strengthen: Fill each function with a leader who has SaaS experience.

items.item: Key employees have employment agreements and a retention or equity plan

benchmarks.4: Agreements, retention plan, and option pool
benchmarks.5: Agreements, retention plan, and option pool

items.why_buyers_care: Buyers want the people who built the product to stay through the transition.
items.concern_if_missing: Unretained key staff become a closing condition or a holdback.
items.what_to_strengthen: Put key people on agreements with a retention bonus that vests after close.

items.item: An org chart shows every role and reporting line
items.why_buyers_care: The org chart is the buyer's map of who does what and where the founder sits.
items.concern_if_missing: No org chart signals that the founder holds the structure in their head.
items.what_to_strengthen: Draw the chart, include contractors, and update it quarterly.

items.item: Hiring and onboarding follow a documented process
items.why_buyers_care: A buyer who plans to grow needs to hire without you.
items.concern_if_missing: Ad-hoc hiring means the growth plan depends on the founder's network.
items.what_to_strengthen: Document the hiring steps and the 30-day onboarding plan for each role type.

items.item: The product is cloud-hosted and multi-tenant, with no on-premise installs
items.why_buyers_care: Delivery model sets margin and scalability. Buyers pay the SaaS multiple for cloud-native products.
items.concern_if_missing: On-prem or single-tenant installs move you toward a software license multiple.
items.what_to_strengthen: Migrate remaining installs to the cloud platform and sunset the legacy option.

items.item: Code is in version control with a repeatable deployment and automated tests

benchmarks.3: CI/CD and test coverage on critical paths

items.why_buyers_care: Technical diligence starts with the repo. Buyers look for process, not perfection.
items.concern_if_missing: No tests or manual deploys raise the technical risk score and the integration cost.
items.what_to_strengthen: Set up CI/CD and cover the critical paths with automated tests.

items.item: Architecture and operations are documented well enough for a new engineer to deploy within a week
items.why_buyers_care: Documentation is how the buyer's team takes over the codebase.
items.concern_if_missing: Undocumented systems extend the founder's required stay.
items.what_to_strengthen: Write the architecture overview, the runbooks, and the environment setup guide.

items.item: Third-party dependencies and open-source licenses are inventoried

benchmarks.2: License inventory current; no unresolved copyleft
benchmarks.3: License inventory current; no unresolved copyleft
benchmarks.4: License inventory current; no unresolved copyleft
benchmarks.5: License inventory current; no unresolved copyleft

items.why_buyers_care: Buyers scan for copyleft licenses and unlicensed components. A finding can block a stock deal.
items.concern_if_missing: An unknown GPL dependency in the core product is a closing condition.
items.what_to_strengthen: Run a license scan and resolve any copyleft or unlicensed component.

items.item: Security meets the benchmark for your size

benchmarks.3: Security policy and annual penetration test

items.why_buyers_care: Security findings in diligence become price reductions or indemnities.
items.concern_if_missing: No security controls at any size is a deal risk; no SOC 2 above $5M blocks many buyers.
items.what_to_strengthen: Start with MFA, backups, and access control; add a penetration test and SOC 2 as you grow.

items.item: Uptime is tracked and meets the benchmark
items.why_buyers_care: Reliability is a retention driver and a contractual obligation in enterprise deals.
items.concern_if_missing: No uptime record means the buyer cannot verify the SLA you sell.
items.what_to_strengthen: Add monitoring and publish uptime to customers.

items.item: A written 12-month product roadmap exists
items.why_buyers_care: The roadmap is the buyer's view of where growth comes from after close.
items.concern_if_missing: No roadmap means the buyer values the product as it is today.
items.what_to_strengthen: Write a 12-month roadmap tied to retention and expansion goals.

items.item: Differentiation is evidenced with win/loss data or documented reasons customers chose you
items.why_buyers_care: Buyers pay a premium for a product that is hard to replace. Claims need evidence.
items.concern_if_missing: Differentiation without evidence reads as marketing, not as a moat.
items.what_to_strengthen: Track win/loss reasons in the CRM and collect 5 customer quotes on why they switched.

items.item: Integrations or an API create switching costs

benchmarks.3: 3+ live integrations or a public API
benchmarks.4: 3+ live integrations or a public API
benchmarks.5: 3+ live integrations or a public API

items.why_buyers_care: Switching costs protect retention and pricing. Buyers model them as a retention floor.
items.concern_if_missing: A product with no integrations is easier to replace at renewal.
items.what_to_strengthen: Build the 3 integrations your customers ask for most and publish an API.

items.item: The ideal customer profile is written down with segment, size, and average contract value

benchmarks.1: ICP documented; 70%+ of new customers match
benchmarks.2: ICP documented; 70%+ of new customers match
benchmarks.3: ICP documented; 70%+ of new customers match
benchmarks.4: ICP documented; 70%+ of new customers match
benchmarks.5: ICP documented; 70%+ of new customers match

items.why_buyers_care: A clear ICP lets a buyer judge the market and the growth plan. It also explains your churn.
items.concern_if_missing: No ICP means the buyer cannot size the opportunity or trust the CAC.
items.what_to_strengthen: Write a 1-page ICP and check that 70%+ of new customers match it.

items.item: A bottom-up TAM and SAM exist with sources
items.why_buyers_care: Buyers pay for headroom. A small or vague TAM caps the multiple even with strong metrics.
items.concern_if_missing: Top-down TAM from a market report is discounted; bottom-up numbers are trusted.
items.what_to_strengthen: Build TAM from ICP count times ACV and cite the sources.

items.item: Market growth is cited from a third-party source

benchmarks.3: 10%+ market growth with a cited source
benchmarks.4: 10%+ market growth with a cited source
benchmarks.5: 10%+ market growth with a cited source

items.why_buyers_care: A growing market gives the buyer tailwind for the growth plan.
items.concern_if_missing: Founder estimates of market growth are not used in buyer models.
items.what_to_strengthen: Cite a Gartner, Forrester, or PitchBook growth rate for your segment.

items.item: Named competitors and your position against them are documented, with win rate

benchmarks.3: Competitor map and 12 months of win rate
benchmarks.4: Competitor map and 12 months of win rate
benchmarks.5: Competitor map and 12 months of win rate

items.why_buyers_care: Buyers want to know who you beat and why. Win rate is the proof.
items.concern_if_missing: No competitive data means the buyer runs their own analysis and prices the unknown.
items.what_to_strengthen: Keep a competitor map and track win rate against each named competitor.

items.item: Recent acquisitions in your category are tracked
items.why_buyers_care: Buyer activity in your category sets the comparable multiples.
items.concern_if_missing: No comparables leaves the buyer to anchor on a generic SaaS multiple.
items.what_to_strengthen: Keep a list of the last 10 deals in your category with price and multiple where public.

items.item: The company is a corporation or LLC with a clean cap table and current founder agreements

benchmarks.1: Cap table and founder agreements current
benchmarks.2: Cap table and founder agreements current
benchmarks.3: Cap table and founder agreements current

items.why_buyers_care: Buyers buy a legal entity. Ownership must be clear before a letter of intent.
items.concern_if_missing: Unclear ownership or a missing founder agreement stops the deal at diligence.
items.what_to_strengthen: Confirm the cap table with counsel and sign any missing founder or shareholder agreement.

items.item: Every employee and contractor who wrote code has signed an IP assignment
items.why_buyers_care: Without IP assignment the company does not own its own product.
items.concern_if_missing: One missing assignment from an early contractor is a closing condition and a holdback.
items.what_to_strengthen: Audit contributors and collect signed assignments from each one.

items.item: Terms of service, privacy policy, and data processing terms are current
items.why_buyers_care: Customer terms set what the buyer inherits, including liability and data rights.
items.concern_if_missing: Outdated terms raise privacy liability and may block enterprise customers from transferring.
items.what_to_strengthen: Update terms with counsel and have every customer accept the current version.

items.item: Trademarks are registered and all domains are owned by the company

benchmarks.2: Mark registered; domains in company account
benchmarks.3: Mark registered; domains in company account
benchmarks.4: Mark registered; domains in company account
benchmarks.5: Mark registered; domains in company account

items.why_buyers_care: Brand assets must transfer with the company.
items.concern_if_missing: A domain in the founder's personal account becomes a transfer item at close.
items.what_to_strengthen: Register the mark and move domains into a company-owned account.

items.item: No open litigation, claims, or regulatory issues
items.why_buyers_care: Buyers price open claims at the worst case and ask for an indemnity.
items.concern_if_missing: Any open claim becomes an escrow at close.
items.what_to_strengthen: Settle or document every open matter before you go to market.

items.item: Vendor and partner contracts are assignable on a change of control
items.why_buyers_care: Critical vendors who can terminate at close give them leverage over your deal.
items.concern_if_missing: A non-assignable hosting or data contract is a closing condition.
items.what_to_strengthen: Review the top 10 vendor contracts and amend the change-of-control clauses.

items.item: Compliance obligations for your vertical are met (GDPR, HIPAA, PCI, or others that apply)

benchmarks.3: Compliance map current; no open gaps
benchmarks.4: Compliance map current; no open gaps
benchmarks.5: Compliance map current; no open gaps

items.why_buyers_care: Regulatory gaps are indemnity items. Enterprise buyers verify them before the LOI.
items.concern_if_missing: A compliance gap in a regulated vertical removes strategic buyers from the process.
items.what_to_strengthen: Map the regulations that apply and close each gap with counsel.

items.item: A data inventory shows where customer data lives and who can access it
items.why_buyers_care: Data diligence asks this question first. The answer sets the privacy risk.
items.concern_if_missing: Unknown data locations extend diligence and raise the privacy indemnity.
items.what_to_strengthen: Document every system that holds customer data and the access list for each.
